paper_title: Corner contribution to the entanglement in two-dimensional systems: A tensor network perspective (Feldman, 2026, arXiv)
deeper_reasoning_2:
\textbf{Claim.} Let \(\Omega:=[0,2\pi)\times[0,a)^2\) be the orientation-and-origin space with normalized uniform measure \(\mu\). Suppose the pointwise crossed-leg count obeys
\[
\log N_A(\theta,r,a,\omega)\leq n_{\mathrm{legs}}(\theta,r,a,\omega)\log\chi
\]
for every \(\omega\in\Omega\), and suppose the averaged count has the fitted form
\[
\overline{n}_{\mathrm{legs}}(\theta,r,a)=\alpha_{\mathrm{legs}}(r,a)+\beta_{\mathrm{legs}}(r,a)(\pi-\theta)\cot\theta.
\]
Then the smooth-subtracted averaged logarithmic Schmidt-rank bound is proportional to
\[
g(\theta):=1+(\pi-\theta)\cot\theta.
\]
If \(\beta_{\mathrm{legs}}(r,a)\) is independent of \(r\) in the continuum-refinement comparison, then the angular coefficient of this averaged logarithmic bound is also independent of \(r\).

\textbf{Premises.}
\begin{align*}
\text{(P1)}\quad &\mu(\Omega)=1.\\
\text{(P2)}\quad &\log N_A(\theta,r,a,\omega)\leq n_{\mathrm{legs}}(\theta,r,a,\omega)\log\chi.\\
\text{(P3)}\quad &\overline{n}_{\mathrm{legs}}(\theta,r,a):=\int_{\Omega}n_{\mathrm{legs}}(\theta,r,a,\omega)\,d\mu(\omega).\\
\text{(P4)}\quad &\overline{n}_{\mathrm{legs}}(\theta,r,a)=\alpha_{\mathrm{legs}}(r,a)+\beta_{\mathrm{legs}}(r,a)h(\theta).\\
\text{(P5)}\quad &h(\theta):=(\pi-\theta)\cot\theta,
\qquad g(\theta):=1+h(\theta).\\
\text{(P6)}\quad &\lim_{\varphi\to\pi}h(\varphi)=-1.\\
\text{(P7)}\quad &\log\chi\text{ is independent of }\theta\text{ and }r.
\end{align*}

\textbf{Derivation.}
Integrating the pointwise bound over \(\Omega\) gives
\begin{align*}
\int_{\Omega}\log N_A(\theta,r,a,\omega)\,d\mu(\omega)
&\leq \int_{\Omega}n_{\mathrm{legs}}(\theta,r,a,\omega)\log\chi\,d\mu(\omega)
&&\text{by (P2)}\\
&=\overline{n}_{\mathrm{legs}}(\theta,r,a)\log\chi
&&\text{by (P3), (P7)}.
\end{align*}
This is the valid averaged logarithmic statement: it bounds the averaged logarithmic Schmidt-rank estimate, not the pointwise value at every single orientation and origin by the averaged count.

Define the smooth reference value by the one-sided limit
\begin{align*}
\overline{n}_{\mathrm{legs}}^{\mathrm{sm}}(r,a)
&:=\lim_{\varphi\to\pi}\overline{n}_{\mathrm{legs}}(\varphi,r,a).
\end{align*}
Using (P4)--(P6),
\begin{align*}
\overline{n}_{\mathrm{legs}}^{\mathrm{sm}}(r,a)
&=\alpha_{\mathrm{legs}}(r,a)-\beta_{\mathrm{legs}}(r,a).
\end{align*}
Define the smooth-subtracted averaged bound contribution by
\begin{align*}
B_{\mathrm{legs}}(\theta,r,a)
&:=\bigl(\overline{n}_{\mathrm{legs}}(\theta,r,a)-\overline{n}_{\mathrm{legs}}^{\mathrm{sm}}(r,a)\bigr)\log\chi.
\end{align*}
Then
\begin{align*}
B_{\mathrm{legs}}(\theta,r,a)
&=\beta_{\mathrm{legs}}(r,a)\bigl(h(\theta)+1\bigr)\log\chi\\
&=\beta_{\mathrm{legs}}(r,a)\log\chi\,g(\theta)
&&\text{by (P5)}.
\end{align*}
Thus the smooth-subtracted angular coefficient is
\begin{align*}
K_{\mathrm{legs}}^{\mathrm{signed}}(r,a)=\beta_{\mathrm{legs}}(r,a)\log\chi.
\end{align*}
Taking the radius derivative where the fitted coefficient is differentiable,
\begin{align*}
\frac{\partial K_{\mathrm{legs}}^{\mathrm{signed}}}{\partial r}
&=\frac{\partial\beta_{\mathrm{legs}}}{\partial r}\log\chi
+\beta_{\mathrm{legs}}\frac{\partial}{\partial r}\log\chi\\
&=\frac{\partial\beta_{\mathrm{legs}}}{\partial r}\log\chi.
\end{align*}
Therefore, if \(\partial\beta_{\mathrm{legs}}/\partial r=0\), then \(\partial K_{\mathrm{legs}}^{\mathrm{signed}}/\partial r=0\). The continuum convention
\begin{align*}
b_A(\theta)=-C g(\theta)
\end{align*}
is matched by setting \(C=-\beta_{\mathrm{legs}}\log\chi\) when this signed constant is positive; otherwise the same angular basis is still the fitted object, with the opposite sign convention.

\textbf{Final Result.}
\[
\boxed{B_{\mathrm{legs}}(\theta,r,a)=\beta_{\mathrm{legs}}(r,a)\log\chi\,\bigl(1+(\pi-\theta)\cot\theta\bigr)}
\]
\hfill$\blacksquare$
deeper_reasoning_3:
\textbf{Claim.} The near-apex skipped-bond probability
\[
p_{\mathrm{skip}}(\theta)=\frac14\bigl(1-(\pi-\theta)\cot\theta\bigr)
\]
generates exactly the smooth-subtracted continuum angular factor. More precisely, if a local contribution to the averaged crossed-leg count has the form
\[
q_{\mathrm{skip}}(\theta,r,a)=c(r,a)+m(r,a)p_{\mathrm{skip}}(\theta),
\]
then its smooth-subtracted part is
\[
q_{\mathrm{skip}}(\theta,r,a)-q_{\mathrm{skip}}^{\mathrm{sm}}(r,a)
=-\frac{m(r,a)}{4}\bigl(1+(\pi-\theta)\cot\theta\bigr),
\]
where \(q_{\mathrm{skip}}^{\mathrm{sm}}(r,a):=\lim_{\varphi\to\pi}q_{\mathrm{skip}}(\varphi,r,a)\). It has the same sharp-corner divergence and smooth-corner quadratic vanishing as the gapped continuum factor.

\textbf{Premises.}
\begin{align*}
\text{(P1)}\quad &p_{\mathrm{skip}}(\theta)=\frac14\bigl(1-h(\theta)\bigr),
\qquad h(\theta):=(\pi-\theta)\cot\theta.\\
\text{(P2)}\quad &g(\theta):=1+h(\theta).\\
\text{(P3)}\quad &\lim_{\theta\to\pi}h(\theta)=-1.\\
\text{(P4)}\quad &q_{\mathrm{skip}}(\theta,r,a)=c(r,a)+m(r,a)p_{\mathrm{skip}}(\theta).\\
\text{(P5)}\quad &g(\theta)=\frac{\pi}{\theta}+O(\theta)\quad(\theta\to0).\\
\text{(P6)}\quad &g(\theta)=\frac13(\pi-\theta)^2+O\bigl((\pi-\theta)^4\bigr)\quad(\theta\to\pi).\\
\text{(P7)}\quad &m(r,a)\text{ is independent of }\theta.
\end{align*}

\textbf{Derivation.}
First evaluate the smooth-angle probability by limit:
\begin{align*}
p_{\mathrm{skip}}^{\mathrm{sm}}
&:=\lim_{\varphi\to\pi}p_{\mathrm{skip}}(\varphi)\\
&=\frac14\left(1-\lim_{\varphi\to\pi}h(\varphi)\right)\\
&=\frac14(1-(-1))
&&\text{by (P3)}\\
&=\frac12.
\end{align*}
Therefore
\begin{align*}
p_{\mathrm{skip}}(\theta)-p_{\mathrm{skip}}^{\mathrm{sm}}
&=\frac14\bigl(1-h(\theta)\bigr)-\frac12\\
&=-\frac14\bigl(1+h(\theta)\bigr)\\
&=-\frac14g(\theta).
&&\text{by (P2)}
\end{align*}
Using (P4), the smooth reference local count is
\begin{align*}
q_{\mathrm{skip}}^{\mathrm{sm}}(r,a)
&=c(r,a)+m(r,a)p_{\mathrm{skip}}^{\mathrm{sm}}.
\end{align*}
Hence
\begin{align*}
q_{\mathrm{skip}}(\theta,r,a)-q_{\mathrm{skip}}^{\mathrm{sm}}(r,a)
&=m(r,a)\bigl(p_{\mathrm{skip}}(\theta)-p_{\mathrm{skip}}^{\mathrm{sm}}\bigr)\\
&=-\frac{m(r,a)}{4}g(\theta)\\
&=-\frac{m(r,a)}{4}\bigl(1+(\pi-\theta)\cot\theta\bigr).
\end{align*}
The endpoint behaviour follows immediately from (P5)--(P7):
\begin{align*}
q_{\mathrm{skip}}(\theta,r,a)-q_{\mathrm{skip}}^{\mathrm{sm}}(r,a)
&=-\frac{m(r,a)\pi}{4\theta}+O(\theta)
&&\text{as }\theta\to0,\\
q_{\mathrm{skip}}(\theta,r,a)-q_{\mathrm{skip}}^{\mathrm{sm}}(r,a)
&=-\frac{m(r,a)}{12}(\pi-\theta)^2+O\bigl((\pi-\theta)^4\bigr)
&&\text{as }\theta\to\pi.
\end{align*}

\textbf{Final Result.}
\[
\boxed{q_{\mathrm{skip}}(\theta,r,a)-q_{\mathrm{skip}}^{\mathrm{sm}}(r,a)
=-\frac{m(r,a)}{4}\bigl(1+(\pi-\theta)\cot\theta\bigr)}
\]
\hfill$\blacksquare$
deeper_reasoning_4:
\textbf{Claim.} The near-smooth lattice-corner probability decomposes into a continuum-shaped part plus an analytic even remainder without relying on endpoint shorthand. Define
\[
p_{\mathrm{skip}}^{\mathrm{sm}}:=\lim_{\varphi\to\pi}p_{\mathrm{skip}}(\varphi),
\qquad
p_{\mathrm{corner}}^{\mathrm{sm}}:=\lim_{\varphi\to\pi}p_{\mathrm{corner}}(\varphi).
\]
With
\[
p_{\mathrm{corner}}(\theta):=\log\bigl(\cos(\pi-\theta)\bigr)-2p_{\mathrm{skip}}(\theta),
\qquad
p_{\mathrm{skip}}(\theta):=\frac14\bigl(1-(\pi-\theta)\cot\theta\bigr),
\]
one has, as a near-smooth identity,
\[
p_{\mathrm{corner}}(\theta)-p_{\mathrm{corner}}^{\mathrm{sm}}
=\frac12\bigl(1+(\pi-\theta)\cot\theta\bigr)+\log\bigl(\cos(\pi-\theta)\bigr).
\]
Consequently,
\[
p_{\mathrm{corner}}(\theta)-p_{\mathrm{corner}}^{\mathrm{sm}}
=-\frac13(\pi-\theta)^2-\frac{13}{180}(\pi-\theta)^4+O\bigl((\pi-\theta)^6\bigr)
\quad(\theta\to\pi).
\]

\textbf{Premises.}
\begin{align*}
\text{(P1)}\quad &\delta:=\pi-\theta.\\
\text{(P2)}\quad &p_{\mathrm{skip}}(\theta):=\frac14\bigl(1-(\pi-\theta)\cot\theta\bigr).\\
\text{(P3)}\quad &p_{\mathrm{corner}}(\theta):=\log(\cos\delta)-2p_{\mathrm{skip}}(\theta).\\
\text{(P4)}\quad &g(\theta):=1+(\pi-\theta)\cot\theta.\\
\text{(P5)}\quad &p_{\mathrm{skip}}(\theta)-p_{\mathrm{skip}}^{\mathrm{sm}}=-\frac14 g(\theta),
\qquad p_{\mathrm{skip}}^{\mathrm{sm}}:=\lim_{\varphi\to\pi}p_{\mathrm{skip}}(\varphi)=\frac12.\\
\text{(P6)}\quad &\log(\cos\delta)=-\frac{\delta^2}{2}-\frac{\delta^4}{12}+O(\delta^6).\\
\text{(P7)}\quad &g(\pi-\delta)=\frac{\delta^2}{3}+\frac{\delta^4}{45}+O(\delta^6).
\end{align*}

\textbf{Derivation.}
First evaluate the smooth-angle corner value by limit, not by assigning an endpoint value inside the open angular domain:
\begin{align*}
p_{\mathrm{corner}}^{\mathrm{sm}}
&:=\lim_{\varphi\to\pi}p_{\mathrm{corner}}(\varphi)\\
&=\lim_{\delta\to0}\left(\log(\cos\delta)-2p_{\mathrm{skip}}(\pi-\delta)\right)\\
&=0-2p_{\mathrm{skip}}^{\mathrm{sm}}\\
&=-1
&&\text{by (P5)}.
\end{align*}
Subtracting this limiting smooth value gives
\begin{align*}
p_{\mathrm{corner}}(\theta)-p_{\mathrm{corner}}^{\mathrm{sm}}
&=\log(\cos\delta)-2p_{\mathrm{skip}}(\theta)+1\\
&=\log(\cos\delta)-2\bigl(p_{\mathrm{skip}}(\theta)-p_{\mathrm{skip}}^{\mathrm{sm}}\bigr)
&&\text{because }2p_{\mathrm{skip}}^{\mathrm{sm}}=1\\
&=\log(\cos\delta)+\frac12g(\theta)
&&\text{by (P5)}\\
&=\frac12\bigl(1+(\pi-\theta)\cot\theta\bigr)+\log\bigl(\cos(\pi-\theta)\bigr)
&&\text{by (P1), (P4)}.
\end{align*}
Now use \(\theta=\pi-\delta\). By (P6) and (P7),
\begin{align*}
p_{\mathrm{corner}}(\pi-\delta)-p_{\mathrm{corner}}^{\mathrm{sm}}
&=\left(-\frac{\delta^2}{2}-\frac{\delta^4}{12}+O(\delta^6)\right)
+\frac12\left(\frac{\delta^2}{3}+\frac{\delta^4}{45}+O(\delta^6)\right)\\
&=-\frac{\delta^2}{3}-\frac{13\delta^4}{180}+O(\delta^6).
\end{align*}
Replacing \(\delta\) by \(\pi-\theta\) gives the claimed expansion. The displayed decomposition also shows why the lattice-corner calculation supports the same angular basis as the crossed-leg calculation while retaining an analytic near-smooth remainder.

\textbf{Final Result.}
\[
\boxed{p_{\mathrm{corner}}(\theta)-p_{\mathrm{corner}}^{\mathrm{sm}}
=\frac12\bigl(1+(\pi-\theta)\cot\theta\bigr)+\log\bigl(\cos(\pi-\theta)\bigr)}
\]
\[
\boxed{p_{\mathrm{corner}}(\theta)-p_{\mathrm{corner}}^{\mathrm{sm}}
=-\frac13(\pi-\theta)^2-\frac{13}{180}(\pi-\theta)^4+O\bigl((\pi-\theta)^6\bigr)}
\]
\hfill$\blacksquare$
deeper_reasoning_5:
\textbf{Claim.} Suppose the orientation-and-origin averaged crossed-leg and lattice-corner counts have fitted forms
\[
\overline{n}_{x}(\theta,r,a)=\alpha_x(r,a)+\beta_x(r,a)(\pi-\theta)\cot\theta,
\qquad x\in\{\mathrm{legs},\mathrm{corners}\}.
\]
If the logarithmic entanglement or counting contribution is a linear combination
\[
T(\theta,r,a)=\lambda_{\mathrm{legs}}\overline{n}_{\mathrm{legs}}(\theta,r,a)
+\lambda_{\mathrm{corners}}\overline{n}_{\mathrm{corners}}(\theta,r,a),
\]
where \(\lambda_{\mathrm{legs}}\) and \(\lambda_{\mathrm{corners}}\) are independent of \(\theta\) and \(r\), then its smooth-subtracted angular component is again proportional to
\[
g(\theta):=1+(\pi-\theta)\cot\theta.
\]
The combined angular coefficient is the sum of the two fitted coefficients weighted by the two physical prefactors.

\textbf{Premises.}
\begin{align*}
\text{(P1)}\quad &x\in\{\mathrm{legs},\mathrm{corners}\}.\\
\text{(P2)}\quad &\overline{n}_{x}(\theta,r,a)=\alpha_x(r,a)+\beta_x(r,a)h(\theta).\\
\text{(P3)}\quad &h(\theta):=(\pi-\theta)\cot\theta,
\qquad g(\theta):=1+h(\theta).\\
\text{(P4)}\quad &\lim_{\varphi\to\pi}h(\varphi)=-1.\\
\text{(P5)}\quad &T(\theta,r,a)=\lambda_{\mathrm{legs}}\overline{n}_{\mathrm{legs}}(\theta,r,a)
+\lambda_{\mathrm{corners}}\overline{n}_{\mathrm{corners}}(\theta,r,a).\\
\text{(P6)}\quad &\lambda_{\mathrm{legs}},\lambda_{\mathrm{corners}}\text{ are independent of }\theta\text{ and }r.
\end{align*}

\textbf{Derivation.}
Define the smooth reference by
\begin{align*}
T^{\mathrm{sm}}(r,a)&:=\lim_{\varphi\to\pi}T(\varphi,r,a).
\end{align*}
Then, by (P5) and linearity of the limit,
\begin{align*}
T(\theta,r,a)-T^{\mathrm{sm}}(r,a)
&=\lambda_{\mathrm{legs}}\left(\overline{n}_{\mathrm{legs}}(\theta,r,a)-\lim_{\varphi\to\pi}\overline{n}_{\mathrm{legs}}(\varphi,r,a)\right)\\
&\quad+\lambda_{\mathrm{corners}}\left(\overline{n}_{\mathrm{corners}}(\theta,r,a)-\lim_{\varphi\to\pi}\overline{n}_{\mathrm{corners}}(\varphi,r,a)\right).
\end{align*}
For each \(x\), (P2)--(P4) give
\begin{align*}
\overline{n}_{x}(\theta,r,a)-\lim_{\varphi\to\pi}\overline{n}_{x}(\varphi,r,a)
&=\beta_x(r,a)\left(h(\theta)-\lim_{\varphi\to\pi}h(\varphi)\right)\\
&=\beta_x(r,a)\bigl(h(\theta)+1\bigr)\\
&=\beta_x(r,a)g(\theta).
\end{align*}
Substituting this identity for \(x=\mathrm{legs}\) and \(x=\mathrm{corners}\) yields
\begin{align*}
T(\theta,r,a)-T^{\mathrm{sm}}(r,a)
&=\bigl(\lambda_{\mathrm{legs}}\beta_{\mathrm{legs}}(r,a)
+\lambda_{\mathrm{corners}}\beta_{\mathrm{corners}}(r,a)\bigr)g(\theta).
\end{align*}
If \(\partial\beta_{\mathrm{legs}}/\partial r=0\) and \(\partial\beta_{\mathrm{corners}}/\partial r=0\), then by (P6),
\begin{align*}
\frac{\partial}{\partial r}
\bigl(\lambda_{\mathrm{legs}}\beta_{\mathrm{legs}}
+\lambda_{\mathrm{corners}}\beta_{\mathrm{corners}}\bigr)
=0.
\end{align*}
Thus the combined angular coefficient is radius-independent under the same fitted-coefficient condition. If
\begin{align*}
\lambda_{\mathrm{legs}}\beta_{\mathrm{legs}}
+\lambda_{\mathrm{corners}}\beta_{\mathrm{corners}}=0,
\end{align*}
then the two fitted angular contributions cancel; otherwise the joint contribution retains the continuum-shaped angular factor.

\textbf{Final Result.}
\[
\boxed{T(\theta,r,a)-T^{\mathrm{sm}}(r,a)=
\bigl(\lambda_{\mathrm{legs}}\beta_{\mathrm{legs}}(r,a)
+\lambda_{\mathrm{corners}}\beta_{\mathrm{corners}}(r,a)\bigr)
\bigl(1+(\pi-\theta)\cot\theta\bigr)}
\]
\hfill$\blacksquare$
deeper_reasoning_8:
\textbf{Claim.} Least-squares fitting commutes with the orientation-and-origin averaging used in the paper. Let \(\Omega\) be the orientation-and-origin space with normalized measure \(\mu\), and let
\[
\overline{n}(\theta):=\int_{\Omega}n(\theta,\omega)\,d\mu(\omega).
\]
For the fitting basis \(h(\theta):=(\pi-\theta)\cot\theta\) on a finite interval \(\mathcal{I}\subset(0,\pi)\), denote by \(\beta[f]\) the fitted slope in the least-squares approximation \(f(\theta)\approx \alpha+\beta h(\theta)\). Then
\[
\beta[\overline{n}]=\int_{\Omega}\beta[n_{\omega}]\,d\mu(\omega),
\qquad n_{\omega}(\theta):=n(\theta,\omega).
\]
Thus the coefficient fitted after uniform orientation-and-origin averaging is exactly the uniform average of the orientation-specific fitted coefficients; it is not a pointwise fixed-orientation claim.

\textbf{Premises.}
\begin{align*}
\text{(P1)}\quad &\mu(\Omega)=1.\\
\text{(P2)}\quad &\mathcal{I}\subset(0,\pi)\text{ is finite and }h(\theta):=(\pi-\theta)\cot\theta\text{ is not constant on }\mathcal{I}.\\
\text{(P3)}\quad &\langle f,q\rangle:=\int_{\mathcal{I}}f(\theta)q(\theta)\,d\theta.\\
\text{(P4)}\quad &M[f]:=|\mathcal{I}|^{-1}\int_{\mathcal{I}}f(\theta)\,d\theta,
\qquad \widetilde{f}:=f-M[f].\\
\text{(P5)}\quad &\beta[f]:=\frac{\langle \widetilde{f},\widetilde{h}\rangle}{\langle \widetilde{h},\widetilde{h}\rangle}.\\
\text{(P6)}\quad &\overline{n}(\theta):=\int_{\Omega}n(\theta,\omega)\,d\mu(\omega),
\qquad n_{\omega}(\theta):=n(\theta,\omega).\\
\text{(P7)}\quad &\text{The required }\theta\text{- and }\omega\text{-integrals are finite and may be interchanged.}
\end{align*}

\textbf{Derivation.}
First center the averaged count:
\begin{align*}
\widetilde{\overline{n}}(\theta)
&=\overline{n}(\theta)-M[\overline{n}]\\
&=\int_{\Omega}n(\theta,\omega)\,d\mu(\omega)
-|\mathcal{I}|^{-1}\int_{\mathcal{I}}\int_{\Omega}n(s,\omega)\,d\mu(\omega)\,ds
&&\text{by (P4), (P6)}\\
&=\int_{\Omega}n(\theta,\omega)\,d\mu(\omega)
-\int_{\Omega}|\mathcal{I}|^{-1}\int_{\mathcal{I}}n(s,\omega)\,ds\,d\mu(\omega)
&&\text{by (P7)}\\
&=\int_{\Omega}\bigl(n_{\omega}(\theta)-M[n_{\omega}]\bigr)\,d\mu(\omega)\\
&=\int_{\Omega}\widetilde{n_{\omega}}(\theta)\,d\mu(\omega).
\end{align*}
Using the normal-equation formula for the fitted slope,
\begin{align*}
\beta[\overline{n}]
&=\frac{\langle \widetilde{\overline{n}},\widetilde{h}\rangle}{\langle \widetilde{h},\widetilde{h}\rangle}
&&\text{by (P5)}\\
&=\frac{1}{\langle \widetilde{h},\widetilde{h}\rangle}
\int_{\mathcal{I}}\left(\int_{\Omega}\widetilde{n_{\omega}}(\theta)\,d\mu(\omega)\right)\widetilde{h}(\theta)\,d\theta
&&\text{previous line}\\
&=\int_{\Omega}\frac{\int_{\mathcal{I}}\widetilde{n_{\omega}}(\theta)\widetilde{h}(\theta)\,d\theta}{\langle \widetilde{h},\widetilde{h}\rangle}\,d\mu(\omega)
&&\text{by (P7)}\\
&=\int_{\Omega}\beta[n_{\omega}]\,d\mu(\omega)
&&\text{by (P5)}.
\end{align*}
Therefore the averaged coefficient used for \(\overline{n}_{\mathrm{legs}}\) and \(\overline{n}_{\mathrm{corners}}\) is a linear projection of the uniformly averaged count data. The result supports the claimed averaged construction while explicitly avoiding any assertion that a single fixed \(\omega\) must display the continuum-like angular dependence.

\textbf{Final Result.}
\[
\boxed{\beta\!\left[\int_{\Omega}n(\cdot,\omega)\,d\mu(\omega)\right]
=\int_{\Omega}\beta[n_{\omega}]\,d\mu(\omega)}
\]
\hfill$\blacksquare$

deeper_reasoning_1.title: Exact intercept absorption between fitted lattice basis and continuum angular basis
deeper_reasoning_1.target_goal_component: Supports G1 and G2 by proving that the paper's fitted basis and the gapped-continuum basis differ only by the fitted intercept.
deeper_reasoning_1.goal_alignment: High: formalizes the central comparison to alpha + beta (pi-theta) cot theta and explains why theta-independent constants can be absorbed.
deeper_reasoning_1.scientific_payoff: Prevents a false mismatch between the lattice fit and the continuum expression containing the extra constant 1.
deeper_reasoning_1.nontrivial_advance_over_sources: Turns the informal intercept-absorption statement into an exact least-squares equivalence.
deeper_reasoning_1.formal_sharpness: Uses a finite fitting domain to avoid endpoint-integrability overclaims near theta equals zero.
deeper_reasoning_1.low_value_rejection_audit: Rejected a mere restatement of the continuum corner formula; this entry proves parameterization equivalence.
controlled_external_lemmas: elementary bijection of two-parameter affine models
deeper_reasoning_1.known_residual_risks_and_mitigation: Does not assert that the empirical fit is exact; it only proves that the two bases are equivalent once a fitted h-model is accepted.

deeper_reasoning_2.goal_alignment: High: connects the averaged n_legs fit to the angular part of the logarithmic Schmidt-rank bound.
deeper_reasoning_2.scientific_payoff: Clarifies exactly what the orientation-and-origin averaged count proves at the logarithmic-bound level.
deeper_reasoning_2.nontrivial_advance_over_sources: Combines pointwise PEPS cut bounds with averaged counts and smooth subtraction; the core entries do not make this bridge explicit.
deeper_reasoning_2.formal_sharpness: Uses explicit smooth-angle limits instead of treating h(pi) as an ordinary value; distinguishes averaged logarithmic bounds from pointwise averaged-count substitutions.
deeper_reasoning_2.low_value_rejection_audit: Rejected an exponential-average claim because E[chi^n] is not generally chi^{E[n]}; retained the valid averaged log statement.
controlled_external_lemmas: smooth subtraction at theta equals pi
deeper_reasoning_2.known_residual_risks_and_mitigation: The fitted coefficient's radius independence is conditional on the paper's empirical no-systematic-dependence claim.
deeper_reasoning_2.revision_note: Revised in v2 to remove informal h(pi) shorthand.

deeper_reasoning_4.title: Limit-defined lattice-corner smooth subtraction and analytic remainder
deeper_reasoning_4.goal_alignment: Very high: supports G2 by deriving the lattice-corner smooth-subtracted expression using explicit smooth-angle limits and by isolating the continuum-shaped part from the analytic near-smooth remainder.
deeper_reasoning_4.scientific_payoff: Shows precisely which part has the continuum angular form and which part is a local analytic correction near the smooth limit.

deeper_reasoning_6.title: Critical logarithmic length scaling is outside the fitted counting mechanism
deeper_reasoning_6.target_goal_component: Scope control and excluded critical-system aim
deeper_reasoning_6.goal_alignment: High: preserves the paper goal as a gapped-style area-independent angular correspondence rather than a critical logarithmic-length result.
deeper_reasoning_6.scientific_payoff: Prevents the generated deeper reasoning from overextending the counting argument to MERA-like or fractal critical scaling suggestions.
deeper_reasoning_6.nontrivial_advance_over_sources: Specializes the impossibility argument to the fitted smooth-subtracted geometric coefficient used in the joint G1/G2 synthesis.
deeper_reasoning_6.formal_sharpness: States the nonzero-angle-factor condition and differentiates with respect to boundary length.
deeper_reasoning_6.low_value_rejection_audit: Rejected a speculative route to critical scaling because it is explicitly outside the canonical goal.
deeper_reasoning_6.known_residual_risks_and_mitigation: The result does not rule out other tensor-network geometries; it only rules out this area-independent fitted counting coefficient as a universal critical log-length law.

deeper_reasoning_7.title: Least-squares centering proves area-dependent intercepts do not bias the fitted angular coefficient
deeper_reasoning_7.target_goal_component: Supports G1/G2 fitted coefficient interpretation and the no-systematic-boundary-length-dependence claim
deeper_reasoning_7.goal_alignment: Very high: directly formalizes why theta-independent area/radius terms belong to alpha, while beta measures only the centered angular component.
deeper_reasoning_7.scientific_payoff: Makes the beta-versus-r interpretation sharper by proving that changes in area-law intercepts cannot by themselves create the reported angular coefficient.
deeper_reasoning_7.nontrivial_advance_over_sources: Adds a projection formula and residual bound absent from the core reasoning, strengthening the empirical-fit interpretation without overclaiming exact global counts.
deeper_reasoning_7.formal_sharpness: Requires a finite fitting interval and nonconstant h, and keeps finite-size/numerical residuals as an explicit error term.
deeper_reasoning_7.low_value_rejection_audit: Rejected an unsupported claim that beta is exactly constant for all r; proved instead what least-squares fitting can and cannot identify.
deeper_reasoning_7.known_residual_risks_and_mitigation: Does not prove empirical residuals are small; it bounds their effect conditional on their L2 size and correlation with the angular basis.

deeper_reasoning_8.title: Averaging commutes with fitted angular coefficient extraction
deeper_reasoning_8.target_goal_component: Supports G1, G2, and the methodological claim by proving that the beta extracted from the orientation-and-origin averaged count is the uniform average of orientation-specific fitted betas.
deeper_reasoning_8.goal_alignment: Very high: directly formalizes the goals file requirement that the continuum-like angular dependence belongs to the uniformly averaged construction, not to arbitrary fixed lattice orientations or origins.
deeper_reasoning_8.scientific_payoff: Explains why the paper can fit after averaging and why the resulting beta is the correct target object for the claimed orientation-and-origin averaged correspondence.
deeper_reasoning_8.nontrivial_advance_over_sources: The core reasoning gives count, expansion, and coefficient facts; this entry adds a structural theorem connecting the averaging operation to the fitted coefficient itself.
deeper_reasoning_8.formal_sharpness: High: states finite-integral and interchange assumptions, derives the centered-count identity, and proves beta linearity exactly.
deeper_reasoning_8.low_value_rejection_audit: Avoids a vague restatement that averaging is important; proves the exact linear projection property needed for the methodology.
deeper_reasoning_8.known_residual_risks_and_mitigation: The theorem does not prove the empirical radius-independence of the averaged beta; it proves that the beta being audited is the mathematically correct averaged coefficient.

rejected_low_value_candidates.reason_rejected: Would not add deeper value and would duplicate the source rather than synthesizing across core reasoning and goals.

rejected_low_value_candidates.reason_rejected: The goals describe fitted averaged counts and local endpoint calculations, not a closed-form exact global count theorem.

rejected_low_value_candidates.candidate: Claim that averaged counts imply pointwise bounds for every orientation and origin.
rejected_low_value_candidates.reason_rejected: The valid operation is averaging the logarithmic bound; pointwise replacement by the averaged count would be unjustified.

rejected_low_value_candidates.candidate: Extend the result to critical log |partial A| scaling or other tensor network geometries.
rejected_low_value_candidates.reason_rejected: The goals list these as out-of-scope future directions or excluded aims.

global_alignment_audit.coverage_summary: G1 is covered by entries 1, 2, 3, 5, 6, 7, and 8; G2 is covered by entries 1, 4, 5, 6, 7, and 8; the joint relation is covered by entry 5; least-squares coefficient isolation is covered by entry 7; orientation-and-origin averaging is strengthened by entry 8; scope exclusion is covered by entry 6.
global_alignment_audit.source_alignment_summary: The output uses the core derivations as lemmas and the goals file to select derivations that advance the averaged square-lattice counting interpretation, especially intercept absorption, averaged logarithmic bounds, local skipped/corner probabilities with limit-defined smooth subtraction, joint leg-corner synthesis, least-squares beta isolation, averaging-fit commutation, and critical-scaling scope exclusion.
global_alignment_audit.latex_validation_summary: All reasoning entries are intended to compile with article, amsmath, and amssymb only; v3 was regenerated to remove remaining endpoint-shorthand risk.
global_alignment_audit.risk_posture: Conditional empirical claims are phrased as conditional on fitted-count assumptions rather than promoted to exact global theorems.

known_residual_risks_and_mitigation.risk: The uploaded goal formalization treats no-systematic radius dependence as an empirical fitted-count result, not a symbolic theorem.
known_residual_risks_and_mitigation.mitigation: Every derivation propagates radius-independence conditionally from beta_x rather than deriving it from first principles.

known_residual_risks_and_mitigation.risk: The lattice-corner near-smooth probability contains an analytic log cos remainder, so a pure global h-law would be overstrong.
known_residual_risks_and_mitigation.mitigation: Entry 4 isolates the remainder exactly and limits the claim to near-smooth support plus fitted-count evidence.

known_residual_risks_and_mitigation.risk: Averaging over orientations and origins can be misread as a pointwise statement.
known_residual_risks_and_mitigation.mitigation: Entry 2 explicitly states the valid averaged logarithmic bound and rejects pointwise replacement.

known_residual_risks_and_mitigation.risk: Least-squares beta stability depends on the residual component aligned with the centered angular basis.
known_residual_risks_and_mitigation.mitigation: Entry 7 gives the exact projection formula and Cauchy bound rather than asserting residuals are negligible.

known_residual_risks_and_mitigation.risk: The phrase that correspondence only emerges after averaging could be misread as an unexplained empirical operation.
known_residual_risks_and_mitigation.mitigation: Entry 8 proves that beta extraction is linear in the count profile, so fitting after averaging targets the exact averaged coefficient and does not require a fixed-orientation theorem.
